pdf.name: Q2 market study.pdf

p: The ceramics and tableware market in France — a summary prepared for the “Spring launch” project.
Written by Camille Laurent with support from Studio Nord. Figures as of June 30, 2026.
The tableware market grew 6.8% year over year, driven by direct sales and independent shops.
The average gross margin of workshops reached 41%, up two points thanks to lower energy costs.
Customers aged 25 to 40 now account for 38% of online purchases.
Segment revenue reached €1.6 billion in the second quarter, 6.8% growth over Q2 2025.
Online sales make up 27% of the total, up from 21% two years ago. Trade fairs remain the top acquisition channel for 61% of workshops.
Three players dominate distribution: two shop networks and one specialist marketplace.
Atelier Morel stands out with a margin 6 points above average, thanks to small-batch production.
The average basket is €86, up 9%. Gifts account for 44% of the quarter’s sales.
Loyalty is rising: 31% of customers buy at least twice a year.
List prices rose 3.2% on average, with no visible effect on volumes.
Gross margin remains under pressure on glazed pieces, whose firing cost has doubled since 2023.
Independent shops remain the top channel, ahead of online sales and trade fairs.
Online sales grow mostly in the evening and on weekends; 64% are placed on mobile.
Spring accounts for 28% of annual sales, just behind the holiday season.
A late-March launch catches Mother’s Day and wedding registries.
Raw material costs may rise in the second half.
Kiln delivery times: up to 14 weeks at the main manufacturers.
Launch the collection in late March, with an early preview for loyal customers.
Protect the margin by keeping glazed items to 30% of the range.
Online survey of 1,240 customers and interviews with 22 workshops, June 2 to 26, 2026.
Market figures come from the French crafts observatory and the national statistics office.
Detailed tables by region, the full questionnaire and the list of workshops interviewed.
Contact: Camille Laurent, project lead, camille.laurent@studionord.fr.

answers.a: The average gross margin of workshops is 41% (page 2), up two points. Atelier Morel does 6 points better (page 4).
Two main risks (page 9): higher material costs in the second half and kiln delivery times of up to 14 weeks.

ask.fallback: In short: market up 6.8%, 41% margin, online sales at 27%, spring = 28% of annual sales. Recommendation: launch in late March (page 10).

summary.b:
Here’s the gist of the 12 pages:
1. The market grew 6.8% year over year (p. 3).
2. The average gross margin is 41% (p. 2).
3. Online sales are 27% of sales, 64% of them on mobile (p. 7).
4. Spring accounts for 28% of annual sales (p. 8).
5. Recommendation: launch in late March and keep glazed items to 30% of the range (p. 10).

act.explain: Gross margin is revenue minus the cost of the pieces sold (clay, glaze, firing). At 41%, a bowl sold for €30 leaves €12.30 to pay for the workshop, rent and salaries.
act.summarize: Workshops keep 41 cents of gross margin per euro sold on average, two points better than in 2025.
act.quote: “The average gross margin of workshops reached 41%, up two points.” — Q2 2026 market study, p. 2.

answers: This module computes the shop cart: subtotal, a 10% spring discount from three ceramics, then free shipping above €80.
Two risks: the discount can exceed the subtotal if prices are negative, and shippingFee charges €6.90 for an empty cart.
I suggest three cases: empty cart, two ceramics with no discount, and three €30 ceramics with free shipping.

segs.text: Hi everyone, thanks for coming. Let’s review the spring launch: timeline, booth and budget.
On the workshop side, the 120 pieces of the “Lagon” collection will be ready on April 2, glazing included.
Studio Nord sent us the booth quote: €9,800 excl. tax, setup included. That’s €600 over budget.
We can make up for it by dropping the extra lighting. Julien, are you OK with that?
Yes, the hall lighting is enough if we keep the light oak shelves.
For communication, I suggest three posts a week from March 24, with Camille’s photos.
Decision: launch on April 14, booth approved without lighting, Inès runs the posting schedule.
I’ll send the shop window visuals by Friday.
Next check-in March 21 at 10 AM, same room.

answers: March 14 meeting on the spring launch: collection ready April 2, Studio Nord booth approved without extra lighting, communication from March 24.
Three decisions: launch on April 14, booth quote accepted at €9,800 excl. tax without lighting, Inès runs the posts.
Julien sends the window visuals on Friday, Inès prepares the schedule, Camille provides the photos. Next check-in March 21.

segs.text: I get to the workshop around six, before the light changes.
Every bowl is thrown by hand; it takes about twelve minutes per piece.
The blue glaze comes from a stoneware recipe Julien perfected in 2019.
On Saturdays we sell directly at the market: that’s where we test new shapes.
“Lagon” is the sea seen from above. Forty pieces, no two alike.

answers: A 6 min 40 film about Atelier Morel in five chapters: the workshop, throwing, glazes, the market and the “Lagon” collection.
“Lagon is the sea seen from above” (5:22) and “Every bowl is thrown by hand” (1:06) are the strongest.
Three 30 s clips: 1:02 to 1:32 (throwing), 2:28 to 2:58 (glazes), 5:18 to 5:48 (collection).
